CHIKKAMAGALURU TALUK AND DISTRICT, AS LAPSED IN VIEW OF SECTION 24(2) OF RIGHT TO FAIR COMPENSATION AND TRANSPARENCY IN LAND ACQUISITION, REHABILITATION AND RESETTLEMENT ACT,
2013, AND THERE IS NO VESTING OF THE PETITIONER SAID LAND AND IT IS FREE FROM ACQUISITION.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER None appears for the petitioners.

2. Heard Sri.A.Ravishankar, learned counsel for respondent No.5.
3.
It is seen that the petitioner Nos.1 to 3 herein, on earlier occasion approached this Court.
It is submitted that the petitioner Nos.1 to 3 by filing a memo dated NC: 2023:KHC:37685 25.09.2018 had sought for dismissal of the petition as withdrawn.

Taking note of the resistance by the learned counsel for the respondent Nos.5 to 6 this Court had passed the following orders:
The petitioners in W.P.Nos.37671- 37673/2016 seek leave of this Court for withdrawing the writ petitions conditionally.
Learned counsel for respondent No.5 opposes the grant of leave for unconditional withdrawal stating that the petitioners have abused process of Court.

2. Although the alleged abuse of Court is a serious matter, still after noticing all the facts and circumstances of the case, leave is granted to withdraw the writ petition unconditionally with a warning that no scope shall be given for such allegations.
Accordingly the petition stands dismissed as withdrawn.
Interim order, if any granted earlier shall stand dissolved.
4. Thus, the petition was left to be prosecuted only by the respondent No.4.
Respondent No.4 had earlier filed a W.P.No.11787/2010 which was dismissed.

Being aggrieved by the dismissal order, he had preferred a writ appeal in W.A.No. 33/2014, respondent No.4 herein was NC: 2023:KHC:37685 the appellant in the said appeal had filed a memo seeking withdrawal of the appeal.

Accordingly, the C. N. Sadashivappa vs State Of Karnataka on 11 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55478889/
3 said appeal was dismissed as withdrawn by the Divisional Bench vide order dated 10.09.2018.

sentences.text: 5. Though sufficient opportunity has been granted there has been no representation.

In view of the aforesaid factual aspects of the matter, namely withdrawal of this very petition by respondent No.1 to 3 and the withdrawal of earlier petition respondent No.4 pertaining to the same subject matter,
this Court do not see any purpose in keeping this matter pending more so, when the petitioner No.4 who is the sole petitioner now not showing any interest in prosecuting the matter.
6. Accordingly, petition is dismissed.
